title: Improve bisecting
body:
This PR makes bisecting easier in several ways:

- **Start a bisect from more views.** The bisect menu (`b`) is now also available in the local branches, remote branches, tags, sub-commits and reflog views. This makes it possible to mark a branch or tag as good or bad without checking it out first. Once git knows both a good and a bad commit, lazygit focuses the commits panel, where the bisect continues.
- **Select the commit to test.** Whenever git picks a new commit to test, lazygit selects it. Before, this happened only when you marked the commit to test in lazygit while it was selected. Now it also happens when lazygit starts during a bisect, when you run `git bisect` commands in a terminal, and when the commit is further down than the commits that lazygit loads at first.
- **Select the result.** When the bisect is done, lazygit selects the first bad commit, so that you can look at it right away. Pressing `b` afterwards shows the result again and offers to reset the bisect. Before, the menu offered to mark the commit that you had just marked.
- **Show the log of HEAD until both a good and a bad commit are known.** If you check out another branch to find a commit to mark, the commits panel shows that branch.
- **Focus the commits panel at startup** if a bisect is in progress.
- **Mark the remaining commits correctly.** The "?" marks for the commits that git still has to consider now come from git. They were missing while git tests the merge base of a good and a bad commit on different branches, and early in a long bisect.
- **Fix labels.** Before git has picked a commit to test, the bisect menu names the selected commit instead of calling it the "current commit". Once the bisect is done, the last tested commit shows its mark instead of "current".

title: Avoid conflicts and duplicate lines when moving a patch to an earlier commit
body:
When moving a custom patch to an earlier commit, or into a new commit before the original one, lazygit applies the patch to the earlier commit and then replayed the original commit unchanged. It relied on git noticing during the replay that the patch's changes are already there. This doesn't always work:

- If the patch contains only some of several adjacent added lines, replaying the original commit stops with a conflict.
- If git can place the patch's added lines in two positions because they repeat the line after them, the replay may put them in the other position than the patch did. Git then keeps both copies, and the file ends up containing the patch's lines twice. There's no conflict, so this goes unnoticed.

Fix this by making the rebase pick a copy of the source commit instead. The copy has the same tree, author and message, but its parent is the original parent with the patch applied. Picking it only replays the source commit's changes minus the patch, so git no longer has to recognize the patch as already applied.

title: Keep mailmapped commits visible when filtering by author
body:
## Bug

When a commit author is corrected by `.mailmap`, selecting that commit and filtering by its author can leave the commits list empty, excluding the selected commit itself.

To reproduce:
1. Create a commit as `Legacy Name <old@example.com>`.
2. Add `Canonical Name <new@example.com> Legacy Name <old@example.com>` to `.mailmap`.
3. In the Commits panel, select the commit, press `s`, and choose its author.

## Fix

Read the mailmapped author email with Git's `%aE` format, and use mailmap for author filtering in both normal and reflog commit queries. This keeps the filter aligned with the author identity shown by lazygit, including when `log.mailmap=false`.

## Validation

- Added an integration test that demonstrates the empty result before the fix and retains the selected commit afterward.
- `env -u NO_COLOR just check` passed (unit tests, integration tests, lint, and generated-file check).
- `just build` passed.

title: Reduce allocations when assembling patch lines
body:
### PR Description

Reduce allocations when collecting patch lines in Patch.Lines().
- Preallocate the result slice using self.LineCount(), accounting for all patch headers, hunk headers, and body lines.
- Replace Hunk.allLines() with appendLinesTo(), which appends directly to the result slice instead of allocating an intermediate slice for each hunk.

title: Add pre- and post- external command execution hooks
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I use [atuin](https://github.com/atuinsh/atuin) to track my command history. But atuin has ability to incorporate command history from multiple sources, for example it can track commands issued by coding agents. It would be great if all external commands that lazygit invokes under the hood could be tracked too.

### Describe the solution you'd like

atuin has command line interface to add commands to history. So my goal could be achieved if lazygit could expose pre- and post- external command hooks that could run (another 😁) external commands and pass various arguments to them, for example the text of the command about to be executed, current folder, etc...

The catch here is that to sync pre and post processing, `atuin history start` returns historyid to stdout. That historyId should be passed to `atuin history end` command. So the lazygit hook system should be able to capture data from the pre- hook and pass it to post hook.

Technically, for user commands this could be incorporated into user scripts, but it would have to be done separately for each command - one central place would be much easier to manage.

title: Show line-change counts per commit in the Commits view
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I can't see how big a commit is without opening it.

### Describe the solution you'd like
A new option, off by default:

```yaml
gui:
  showNumstatInCommitsView: false
```

It shows `+N -M` after the commit subject:

```
a1b2c3d4 JD  Add retry logic to HTTP client +42 -7
e5f6a7b8 JD  Fix typo in README +1 -1
```

Adding `--shortstat` to the existing `git log` call is enough, so no extra process is needed. It should be a separate option because, unlike the others, it has a cost: git computes a diff for every loaded commit.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Running `git log --shortstat` outside lazygit.

### Additional context
I couldn't find an earlier request for this. I have a working prototype with a test and can share it as a draft PR.

title: Show line-change counts in the Commit Files view
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When I open a commit, I see its files but not how much each one changed.

### Describe the solution you'd like
A new option, off by default and independent of `showNumstatInFilesView`:

```yaml
gui:
  showNumstatInCommitFilesView: false
```

It shows `+N -M` per file, with sums on directories and the root, like the Files view.

It needs no extra git process: `--name-status` can't be combined with `--numstat`, but `git diff --raw --numstat -z` returns both in one call, and the raw part converts directly to the current `--name-status` format.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
The diffstat at the top of the commit diff, but it isn't next to the file list.

### Additional context
@mark2185 asked for this in #4015, and @stefanhaller replied in https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pull/4015#issuecomment-2468095432 that it would be good, maybe more useful than in the Files view, as a separate option. Nobody followed up, so here's an issue for it. I have a working prototype with tests and can share it as a draft PR.

title: Show summed line-change counts on directories in the Files view
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
With `showNumstatInFilesView`, files show `+N -M`, but directories and the root `/` show nothing, so I can't see the total size of my uncommitted change or of a collapsed folder.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Under the same option, show on each directory (and the root) the sum for all files below it:

```
▼ / +151 -42
  ▼ pkg +120 -30
     M foo.go +100 -20
     M bar.go +20 -10
   M main.go +31 -12
```

No extra git calls needed: it's a sum of the already loaded per-file numbers.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
A custom command with `git diff --shortstat HEAD`, but that's a popup, not always visible.

### Additional context
Suggested by @opus131 in https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/pull/4015#issuecomment-2466249072. I have a working prototype (~10 lines) and can share it as a draft PR.

title: Fix hosting-service links when remote is not named origin
body:
### PR Description

Lazygit always used `remote.origin.url` when building pull-request and commit browser links. If the only remote was named something else (e.g. a personal name instead of `origin`), `git ls-remote --get-url origin` returns the literal string `origin`, which then surfaces as "Unsupported git service".

This change resolves the remote used for hosting-service URLs as follows:

1. If there is exactly one remote, use that remote.
2. If there are multiple remotes, prompt the user to choose one.
3. If there are no remotes, return a clear error.

The same resolution is used for creating/copying pull request URLs and opening/copying commit URLs.

title: Allow config files to import/include other config files (in-file split for custom commands)
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I split complex custom commands into their own files (e.g. all tag-related commands in `tags.yml`, loaded via `LG_CONFIG_FILE=".../config.yml,.../tags.yml"`). This works, but the file list lives outside the config itself: it must be re-declared in every shell/launcher via the env var (or `--use-config-file`), and it grows with each additional split file. There is no way for `config.yml` to pull in another file on its own, so a dotfiles-managed config directory still depends on shell wiring to load completely.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Support an in-file key, e.g. `import: ["tags.yml"]` (paths resolved relative to the importing file), with entries processed in listed order using the exact merge rules `LG_CONFIG_FILE` uses today (per-key override with last-file-wins, `customCommands` appended across files, `Validate()` per file). Cycle safety is cheap: keep a visited set of canonicalized absolute paths (`filepath.Abs` + `EvalSymlinks`) and merge each file once. The existing `loadUserConfig` loop already merges an ordered file list, so this only changes how that list is built.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
- `LG_CONFIG_FILE` comma-separated list (status quo): works, but it is process-global and maintained separately from the files it references.
- Repo-scoped files (`.git/lazygit.yml`, parent-dir `.lazygit.yml`): wrong scope, they are per-repo rather than a global grouping mechanism.

### Additional context
Related history: #1255 (2021) asked about extending/splitting config and was resolved by documenting the `LG_CONFIG_FILE` list; an in-file import was never evaluated there. I searched open and closed issues for "import config include", "include config file", and "multiple config files" and found no duplicate request for an in-file import directive.

title: feat: skipNotInstalled option to silently skip diffRenderers whose tool is missing
body:
## Motivation

Dotfiles shared across machines: some `diffRenderers`' tools aren't
installed everywhere (e.g. `ydiff`). On v0.64.1, cycling `|` onto such a
renderer renders failure in place — the main view shows the tool's
stderr/usage text or nothing at all. Exit codes are ignored: a renderer
exiting 1 still "renders"; its stderr is just merged into the view
(verified with a marker renderer that prints to stderr and exits 1).

## Workaround today

A wrapper script per entry: check `command -v TOOL`, print a warning,
fall back to `cat` (stdinFilter) or exit 0 (extDiff). Works, but every
user must reinvent this boilerplate.

## Proposal

Per-renderer opt-in, e.g.

```yaml
git:
  diffRenderers:
    - command: ydiff -p cat -s --wrap --width={{columnWidth}}
      skipNotInstalled: true
```

When the tool is not found on PATH, silently skip: no missing-tool
warning, render the fallback (or nothing) quietly. Default `false` keeps
current behavior unchanged.

## Notes / open questions

- How is "the tool" derived? First word of `command`?
- extDiff invokes per file via `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`: skip each file's
  render independently?
- Tested on v0.64.1.

title: Redo after undoing cherry-pick, merge or revert does not restore the action commit
body:
### Describe the bug
After a cherry-pick, merge, or revert, pressing `z` and then `Z` does not restore the commit created by the action.

For a cherry-pick, `z` resets to the parent of the picked commit instead of the pre-action HEAD, and `Z` then resets to the pre-action HEAD instead of the cherry-pick commit. Cherry-pick commit is left only in the reflog and is no longer reachable from the branch.

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Run this in an empty directory:
```sh
git init -b main
git config user.name "Repro"
git config user.email "repro@example.com"

printf 'a\n' > f.txt
git add f.txt
git commit -m "A base"

git switch -c feature
printf 'a\nb\n' > f.txt
git add f.txt
git commit -m "B feature"

git switch main
printf 'c\n' > g.txt
git add g.txt
git commit -m "C main"

git cherry-pick feature
```
The resulting history is:
```text
A -- C -- D   (main)
 \
  B           (feature, branched from A)
```

Start lazygit in the repository, then:

1. Press `z`, confirm the undo popup with Enter.
2. Press `Z` (shift+z), confirm the redo popup with Enter.
3. Quit lazygit and inspect the repository.

**Actual behavior**

* After `z`: HEAD is `A`; the command log shows
  `git reset --soft <A>`.
* After `Z`: HEAD is `C`; the command log shows
  `git reset --hard <C>`.
* `D` is no longer on any branch (`git branch --contains <D>` is empty) but is
  still present in the reflog and `git show <D>` still works.

```text
$ git log --oneline --graph --all --decorate
* <C> (HEAD -> main) C main
| * <B> (feature) B feature
|/
* <A> A base

$ git branch --contains <D>
(no output)

$ git show --stat --oneline <D>
<D> B feature
 f.txt | 1 +
```

`D` is only reachable through the reflog, not through any branch.

The reflog also shows the two steps:

```text
$ git reflog --format="%h %gs" -n 8
<C> [lazygit redo]: updating HEAD
<A> [lazygit undo]: updating HEAD
<D> cherry-pick: B feature
<C> commit: C main
<A> checkout: moving from feature to main
<B> commit: B feature
<A> checkout: moving from main to feature
<A> commit (initial): A base
```

### Expected behavior
* `z` should undo the cherry-pick: HEAD goes from `D` to `C`.
* `Z` should redo it: HEAD goes from `C` to `D`.

In other words, undo should restore the old HEAD of the undone reflog entry, and redo should restore the commit created by that entry.

Even if the undo target `A` were considered intentional, the redo is still wrong: the branch is at `A` after the undo, and `Z` moves it to `C` instead of restoring `D`.

The same wrong targets occur for `git merge --no-ff` and `git revert`:

| Operation | Before action | Action commit | After `z` | After `Z` | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cherry-pick | `C` | `D` | `A` | `C` | `z`: `D -> C`, `Z`: `C -> D` |
| merge `--no-ff` | `C` | `M` | `A` | `C` | `z`: `M -> C`, `Z`: `C -> M` |
| revert | `B` | `R` | `A` | `B` | `z`: `R -> B`, `Z`: `B -> R` |

For the revert case, `z` also removes `B` (the commit being reverted) from the branch, so it is not undoing only the revert.

title: Add an option to disable the stacked-branch push prompt
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Since the stacked-branch push support introduced in v0.66.0 (#6045), pushing the current branch can show an additional prompt asking whether to push branches stacked below it too.

For example, when pushing `master`, Lazygit detects a local `wip` branch below it with unpushed commits and offers:

- Push all these branches in addition to the current one
- Push only 'master'
- Cancel

I only want to push the current branch in this workflow. Repeatedly choosing “Push only” adds friction to an otherwise routine action. The first/default choice also offers to push additional branches that I did not intend to publish as part of that action.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Please add a configuration option to disable the stacked-branch push prompt and always push only the current branch, restoring the previous single-branch behavior.

The existing stacked-branch behavior could remain the default. Opting out should retain Lazygit's normal upstream-selection and force-push confirmation handling; it should only skip offering to push other branches.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Selecting “Push only” each time, which is the repetitive interaction I would like to avoid.
- Replacing the push keybinding with a custom command that runs `git push`. This bypasses Lazygit's normal upstream-selection and force-push dialogs as well, so it is not an equivalent replacement.

### Additional context

Observed on Lazygit v0.66.1, Linux, installed through Nix.

title: Improve display and handling of deleted submodules and nested repos/worktrees
body:
Previously, if a submodule was deleted upstream and you pulled the branch, it would show up like this:

```
▼ modules
  ▼ submodule1
    ▼ ??
```

which looks confusing. What's more, selecting the `??` showed "error: Could not access 'modules/submodule1/null'" in the main view, and trying to discard the `??` (which is what you want to do in this situation) did discard the submodule, but then showed an error popup "open modules/submodule1: no such file or directory".

All of this is confusing, so improve it by showing this in the Files panel instead:

```
▼ modules
  ?? submodule1 (removed submodule)
```

and in the main view, show an explanation of what this is, and what you are likely to want to do (which is press `d` to discard it). In addition, it shows the git status of the submodule in case it might contain local modifications that you would lose.

While we're at it, improve the display of nested repos or linked worktrees in a similar way; it is likely that you want to .gitignore these if they are located, say, in an in-repo `worktrees` folder, and the main view now shows this as a hint when you select one.

And finally, prevent staging and committing deleted submodules or nested repositories, because it would result in a broken repo state and is never what you want to do.

title: Difftastic loses all ANSI colours after upgrading from 0.65.1 to 0.66.1

### Describe the bug
Diff output when using Difftastic is now monochrome after updating to 0.66.1 (Windows 11), while it had full colour before.

### To Reproduce
Use difftastic as your external diff tool:
`git config diff.external difft`

Configure LazyGit to use it:
```yaml
git:
  diffRenderers:
    - type: extDiff
      command: difft
```

### Expected behavior
No change in difft output when updating LazyGit

### Version info:
0.66.1

### Terminal info:
Alacritty on Windows 11

Updating my LazyGit config with `--color=always` fixed this, maybe I should have been doing this from the start.
```yaml
git:
  diffRenderers:
    - type: extDiff
      command: difft --color=always --background={{colorScheme}} --context={{diffContext}}
```

title: Restore the terminal more reliably after a panic

labels.name: maintenance
labels.description: For refactorings, CI changes, tests, version bumping, etc

body: We already have a mechanism in place that takes care of restoring the terminal if a panic occurs, but it was not consistently used. Use it for all goroutines, and add a test that guards against forgetting it when we add new ones.

title: Make double-click detection more precise
body:
Lazygit decided whether two clicks form a double click based on the times it handled them. This can lead to false results: if the first click takes the UI thread more then 500ms to handle, then the second click is not detected as a double click even when it happened quickly after the first. Conversely, if two clicks happen a second apart while the main loop is busy, they are handled quickly once the main loop unblocks, and got detected as a double-click.

I never actually ran into either of these problems in practice, and we try hard to prevent lazygit from blocking the UI for longer than necessary. I only noticed this because an integration test that performs a double click occasionally fails when the CI runner is under heavy load.

Fix this by recording the times at which the events were received, and use those for double-click detection.

title: fix(gui): restore complete diff line highlighting support
body:
Fixes #6117

### Problem
In v0.66.x, selecting a line or hunk in the diff pane highlights only the first two and last two columns instead of the full line. This was introduced when `SelectedLineColorWidth` was hardcoded to 2 on `Main` and `Secondary` views, with `view.go` coloring both the left edge and the right boundary without user configurability, degrading usability and accessibility for users who rely on full-line highlight to track hunks.

### Solution
- Prevented spurious right-margin highlight painting when `SelectedLineColorWidth` is used as a left marker.
- Exposed user configurability for diff selected line highlight width, allowing users to restore full-width selection.
- Added test coverage in `pkg/gocui` and `pkg/gui`.

Verified via container sandbox test suite.

title: Improve performance with very long diffs
body: Parsing long diffs was very slow, especially for commits that add or remove files with hundreds of thousands of lines. This caused very noticeable lags for certain operations such as scrolling down in such a diff using `>`, or bringing up the `<ctrl-g>` files menu.

title: Fix diff rendering after scrolling far down
body:
Fix a regression introduced in v0.65.0: if the main view is scrolled more than about 5000 lines down a diff and another commit with a diff of more than 5000 lines is selected, the main view kept showing the previous diff. Switching between the two long commits then didn't update the main view at all. Only selecting a shorter commit would get this unstuck.

Along the way, fix another smaller bug and a performance problem; see commit messages for details.

title: Don't log the diff renderer probe in the command log
body: If a diff renderer is configured, its command shows up in the command log once after startup, although the user didn't do anything. This is the probe that asks the renderer whether it emits OSC 1717 metadata. It changes nothing, so like other read-only commands it shouldn't be logged.

title: Mouse button remains pressed after returning from an editor opened via a delta hyperlink
body:
### Describe the bug

With delta configured as the diff renderer as follows:

```yaml
git:
  diffRenderers:
    - command: delta --dark --paging=never --line-numbers --hyperlinks --hyperlinks-file-link-format="lazygit-edit://{path}:{line}"
```

After opening an editor through a line-number hyperlink and returning to Lazygit, the mouse button appears to remain pressed. In my testing, this happens when using Ghostty or a Ghostty-based terminal emulator such as cmux.

### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Configure the diff renderer in Lazygit as shown above.
2. Open Ghostty, navigate to a repository, and run `lazygit`.
3. Click a line-number hyperlink in the diff view to open the editor (Emacs).
4. Close the editor and return to Lazygit.
5. Move the mouse. All UI elements along the pointer’s path react as if the mouse button were still held down.

### Expected behavior

After returning from the editor, moving the mouse should not cause UI elements along the pointer’s path to be clicked.

### Version info:

```text
commit=, build date=, build source=Homebrew, version=0.66.0, os=darwin, arch=arm64, git version=2.51.1
```

### Terminal info:

- Ghostty 1.3.1
- cmux 0.65.0

The issue did not reproduce with the following terminal:

- Terminal (the default macOS terminal) 2.15

### Additional context

Possibly related to #3928.

title: Allow scrolling the diff view horizontally when gui.wrapLinesInDiffView is off
body:
If gui.wrapLinesInDiffView is false, long lines of a diff run off the right edge of the main view, and there was no way to see the rest of them. This made it hard to see what has changed in such a line. The old staging and patch-building views scrolled sideways with `H` and `L`, but the focused main view that replaced them had no binding for these keys.

Bind them in the focused main view, as in the side panels. Leaving the view scrolls it back to the left edge, as it did for the staging view.

In addition, when jumping to the next search result, and it is past the right edge, scroll sideways to show it. This happens both in the new main view when `gui.wrapLinesInDiffView` is off, but also in side panels, so it is an improvement over pre-0.66 versions there.

title: Fix search match highlighting when a custom patch is active
body:
Search matches beside the inclusion gutter were highlighted in the wrong place, and hovering over or clicking a hyperlink there acted on the wrong cell. The draw loop starts the content after the gutter, but the code that maps a view column back to a column of the content only added the horizontal origin and ignores the gutter.

Add a helper that does both, and use it for search highlights, hover and clicks.

title: Fix double-width characters in the last column drawing over the view's frame
body:
A double-width character that starts in the last column of a view is drawn over the view's frame. One that is scrolled halfway out to the left is skipped, and the column it reaches into isn't drawn at all. The draw loop clips cells against the edges of the view as if every cell were one column wide.

A terminal can't show half of a double-width character. So draw a blank in the column that is on screen, in the character's colors, and let the selection highlight cover that column like any other.

title: Show the diff view's narrow selection bar on the right edge too
body:
This is an improvement for users who use a side-by-side diff renderer on a very large screen; in this scenario it was hard to see which hunk on the right side was selected.

See https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/6098#issuecomment-6064528142.

title: Open files of a branch's diff from the worktree that has it checked out
body:
If you enter a branch in the branches panel and press `e` on a line of a commit's diff, or on a file in the commit files panel entered from there, lazygit opens the file in the current worktree. If another worktree has the branch checked out, this is the wrong copy of the file. The current worktree may have it in a different state, or not have it at all. Clicking a lazygit-edit:// hyperlink of a diff renderer in such a diff has the same problem.

Fix this by opening the file from the worktree that has the branch checked out instead, and carry the line number forward to the file as that worktree has it. If no other worktree has the branch checked out, the file is still opened from the current worktree.

Also, fix the same problem for the `o` command, and for the "Absolute path" entry in the "Copy to clipboard" menu.

Finally, fix a long-standing annoyance when trying to open a file that has since been deleted or renamed; in that case, most editors would create it as a new, empty file, which is not useful. Show an error message in that case instead.

Fixes #6102.

title: Editing a diff line of a branch checked out in another worktree opens the current worktree's copy
body:
### Describe the bug

I opened lazygit in the main worktree and browsed the commits of a branch that a linked worktree has checked out. When I press `e` on a line in that commit's diff, lazygit opens the file from the **current** worktree, not from the worktree where the branch lives. The editor shows the wrong copy of the file, and the line number is adjusted against that copy too.

From reading the code (references are pinned to `c5f7158`, which is both `v0.66.0` and current `master`):

- [`editDiffLine`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/c5f7158154602d23b0750d4304c73e2aead8df5b/pkg/gui/controllers/main_view_controller.go#L1063-L1083) passes the repo-relative `info.Path` to `EditFileAtLine`.
- [`EditFileAtLine`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/c5f7158154602d23b0750d4304c73e2aead8df5b/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/files_helper.go#L31-L38) resolves it with `filepath.Abs`, so the path always ends up in lazygit's own worktree.
- [`AdjustLineNumber`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/c5f7158154602d23b0750d4304c73e2aead8df5b/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/diff_helper.go#L238-L267) runs `git diff <commit> -- <path>` in the current worktree, so the line number is mapped onto the wrong working copy.

Lazygit already knows which worktree has a branch checked out ([`WorktreeForBranch`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/c5f7158154602d23b0750d4304c73e2aead8df5b/pkg/commands/git_commands/worktree.go#L57-L65)), and the Branches panel uses that to offer switching worktrees on checkout.

### To Reproduce

```shell
git init -q main && cd main
mkdir sub && echo a > sub/f.txt && git add . && git commit -qm init
git worktree add -q ../main-feature
cd ../main-feature && echo c >> sub/f.txt && git commit -qam feat
cd ../main
lazygit
```

1. In **Local branches**, select `main-feature` (shown with the worktree icon) and press `<enter>`.
1. Press `<enter>` on the `feat` commit, then on `sub/f.txt`.
1. Focus the main view, move to the `+c` line and press `e`.
1. The editor opens `main/sub/f.txt`.

### Expected behavior

Because `main-feature` is checked out in `../main-feature`, the editor opens `main-feature/sub/f.txt`, with the line number adjusted against that worktree's working copy. This is where the line from the diff actually exists and can be edited.

Pressing `e` on a file in the **Commit files** panel probably has the same problem, since [`CommitFilesController.edit`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/c5f7158154602d23b0750d4304c73e2aead8df5b/pkg/gui/controllers/commits_files_controller.go#L434-L439) also passes repo-relative paths to `EditFiles`. I only verified the diff-line case.

### Screenshots

_Not applicable._

### Version info:

```
commit=, build date=, build source=Homebrew, version=0.66.0, os=darwin, arch=arm64, git version=2.56.0
```

### Terminal info:

tmux 3.7c on macOS, with `os.editPreset: nvim-remote`. I don't think this depends on the terminal or the editor, because the wrong path is already decided before the editor command runs.

### Additional context

To work around it, switch to the branch's worktree in the **Worktrees** tab before editing.

title: Fix typos in gocui docs
body: Fixes two small typos in the vendored gocui docs: `ontop` -> `on top` (README.md) and `adjustement on` -> `adjustments to` (CHANGES_tcell.md). Docs only, no code changes.

title: Show errors for unresolvable diff lines
body: If lazygit can't work out what diff lines it is supposed to act on when staging a hunk (for example because of bugs like the one in #6099, or maybe because of a misbehaving OSC-1717 diff renderer), it used to do nothing and silently ignore the error. Now it shows an error popup to the user in such a case, so that they can report the bug more easily.

title: Feat: add support for multiple-repositories, show a repos list when lazygit starts in a directory of repos
body: ### PR Description When you start lazygit in a directory that is not a git repo but contains repos, lazygit now lists those repos in a new Repositories panel. Before this change, lazygit showed the "not a repository" prompt and it still shows if there's no repos in the subdirs. - Discovery walks down `multiRepo.maxDepth` levels (default 2). It stops at each repo, so it does not list nested repos or submodules. It skips hidden directories and symlinks. - Lazygit opens the first valid repo (sorted by path) and focuses the list. If a repo is broken, for example an empty `.git` or a stale worktree `.git` file, lazygit skips it. - The Repositories panel replaces the Status panel in window 1. `repos` is a new valid tab name for `gui.sidePanels`. If your config lists `repos` already, lazygit uses it as is. - Each row shows the path relative to the start directory, the branch, and `*` if the working tree has changes. The open repo has a marker, like the current worktree in the Worktrees panel. - `space` or `enter` switches to the selected repo. Focus stays on the list. The main view shows `git status` for the selected repo. `e` and `u` from the Status panel work here too, and `ctrl+r` still opens recent repos. - If lazygit finds no repos, the existing `notARepository` behavior runs. `GIT_DIR` and `-p` work as before. Performance: - Lazygit reads branch names from `HEAD` files. Dirty checks run `git status --porcelain` in the background, 8 at a time, with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. So they never take `index.lock` in a repo that you work in, and they do not block a repo switch. - The full list reloads at startup, on a repo switch, and on `R`. Other refreshes update only the row of the open repo. The periodic files refresh does not touch the list. Out of scope for this PR: ahead/behind counts, rebase/merge state per repo, and bulk fetch or pull across repos. Known limitation: a repo switch clears the list filter. All other panels behave the same way on a repo switch. Open question: I replaced the Status panel in this mode because Status shows only the current repo. If you prefer the list as a separate tab next to Status, I can change it, but I think this is a pretty great UX. ### Please check if the PR fulfills these requirements * [x] Cheatsheets are up-to-date (run `go generate ./...`) * [x] Code has been formatted (see [here](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-formatting)) * [x] Tests have been added/updated (see [here](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/master/pkg/integration/README.md) for the integration test guide) * [x] Text is internationalised (see [here](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#internationalisation)) * [x] If a new UserConfig entry was added, make sure it can be hot-reloaded (see [here](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/master/docs/dev/Codebase_Guide.md#using-userconfig)) * [x] Docs have been updated if necessary * [x] You've read through your own file changes for silly mistakes etc I checked these facts against commit e9d515569: - go generate added the "Repositories" section to every docs-master/keybindings/*.md and the new key to Config.md. - The loader reads multiRepo.maxDepth from the config at each full reload, so a changed value takes effect on the next R. - The last checkbox is your own read-through, so I left it unchecked.

title: mnemonicPrefix = true in gitconfig breaks hunk staging
body:
### Describe the bug
Setting `mnemonicPrefix = true` under `[diff]` in gitconfig breaks staging hunks in the latest lazygit. Pressing `space` in the focused diff shows "Apply Patch" in the command log, but nothing gets staged. Discarding and unstaging are affected the same way.

title: Collect signing credentials in lazygit's popup instead of a subprocess terminal (prototype for #6094)
body:
**Draft, and not a merge request.** I've read CONTRIBUTING.md and I'm not asking you to review or merge this. It's here under the second case the guide allows for — a prototype attached to an issue (#6094), published so the change is legible and so anyone else hitting this can pick it up in their own fork. Close it whenever you like; I won't take it personally.

Up front, since the guide raises it directly: this was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). I drove it, and I verified the result on my own hardware with a real YubiKey rather than taking it on faith — the verification notes below are things I actually observed, not predictions. Weigh that however you think is right.

### What it fixes

Signing a commit with a PIN- or passphrase-protected key always costs a subprocess terminal, and `git.overrideGpg` — which looks like the way to avoid it — doesn't prompt at all; it makes signed commits fail outright. Full detail in #6094.

Two commits:

**1. `Match a security key PIN prompt that omits the key path`**

The PIN patterns were written against `ssh`'s wording (`sshconnect2.c`), which names the key path:

```c
xasprintf(&prompt, "Enter PIN for %s key %s: ",
    sshkey_type(sign_key), id->filename);
```

`ssh-keygen` already knows which key it was handed, so it names only the type (`ssh-keygen.c`, `verify-required` branch):

```c
xasprintf(&prompt, "Enter PIN for %s key: ", sshkey_type(signkey));
```

`Enter\s*PIN\s*for\s*.+\s*key\s*.+:` requires at least one character between `key` and `:`, so it matches the first and misses the second. Adds one pattern covering both, plus a test case. It can't over-match — `ttyText` resets at every newline, so the scanner only ever holds the current line.

**2. `Prompt for signing credentials rather than dropping to a subprocess`**

`PromptOnCredentialRequest` sets both `credentialStrategy` and `usePty`, and `Run()` dispatches on the strategy ahead of the streaming path. The sync commands opt in; the gpg helper never did, and discarded the `gocui.Task` the prompt needs. So it opts in.

### Scope, honestly

The first commit isn't separately reachable today — every other call site with a credential strategy (`sync.go`, `remote.go`, `tag.go`) is a network op invoking `ssh`, whose wording carries the path. Only signing goes through `ssh-keygen`, and signing never ran under credential handling. The two commits are really one change; I split them because the regex is a self-contained claim you can check independently.

### Verification

On a `sk-ssh-ed25519` key with `verify-required`, `gpg.format = ssh`, `commit.gpgSign = true`:

- Before: commit drops to the subprocess terminal; with `overrideGpg: true`, commit fails with "Git command failed" and no prompt.
- After, with `overrideGpg: true`: popup → PIN → touch → `git log --show-signature` reports a good signature.
- The new test is a real regression test: red on master, green with the regex commit.
- `go build ./...` clean, `gofmt` clean, `go test ./pkg/commands/oscommands/...` passes.

### Two things I'd flag rather than paper over

- **The touch isn't announced.** After the PIN, the status sits on "Committing…" while the key blinks, because `Confirm user presence for key ...` matches no pattern. Push behaves identically today, so this is at least consistent, but it's a real rough edge.
- **Interactive pre-commit hooks.** Anything else wanting a TTY during the commit now runs under lazygit's pty instead of getting the subprocess terminal. I don't have such a hook to test with, and this is the part I'd want a second opinion on.

I also didn't touch the `overrideGpg` docs or default. Whether this should be gated on that flag at all, or just become the behaviour, is a design call I didn't want to make for you.

Happy to answer questions and stick around on #6094.

title: Signing PIN can't be collected in-TUI: gpg helper never opts into credential handling, and the PIN pattern misses ssh-keygen's wording
body:
**Describe the bug**

Signing a commit with a PIN-protected key always costs a subprocess terminal, even though lazygit already has all the machinery needed to collect that PIN in its own popup. `git.overrideGpg`, which looks like the way out, doesn't prompt at all — it makes signed commits fail outright.

I have a `sk-ssh-ed25519` (FIDO2/YubiKey) signing key with `verify-required`, so every signed commit needs a PIN and a touch:

```
git config gpg.format ssh
git config user.signingKey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_sk_gh.pub
git config commit.gpgSign true
```

- Default config: committing drops to the subprocess terminal to collect the PIN ("Press enter to return to lazygit"). Pushing with the *same* key gets a proper in-TUI popup.
- `git.overrideGpg: true`: the commit fails with "Git command failed" instead of prompting.

**Why**

`GpgHelper.runAndStream` runs the signing command via `cmdObj.StreamOutput().Run()`, so it gets no pty and no credential detection:

https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.61.1/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/gpg_helper.go#L43-L45

But credential handling isn't push-specific — it's a property of the command object. `PromptOnCredentialRequest` sets `credentialStrategy = PROMPT` *and* `usePty = true`, and `Run()` dispatches on the strategy before the streaming path. `sync.go` opts in; `gpg_helper.go` doesn't, and it even discards the `gocui.Task` the prompt needs (`func(gocui.Task) error`).

So `overrideGpg: true` has no way to succeed with a key that asks for anything: it selects the one path that cannot answer.

**Suggested fix**

```diff
-	return self.c.WithWaitingStatus(waitingStatus, func(gocui.Task) error {
-		if err := cmdObj.StreamOutput().Run(); err != nil {
+	return self.c.WithWaitingStatus(waitingStatus, func(task gocui.Task) error {
+		if err := cmdObj.PromptOnCredentialRequest(task).Run(); err != nil {
```

That alone isn't enough, though — it exposes a second problem.

**Second part: the PIN pattern doesn't match `ssh-keygen`'s wording**

With the above, the prompt reaches the command log and then sits there unanswered:

```
Git output:
Enter PIN for ED25519-SK key:
```

The prompt table only matches the wording `ssh` uses, which names the key path:

https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.61.1/pkg/commands/oscommands/cmd_obj_runner.go#L406

```go
`Enter\s*PIN\s*for\s*.+\s*key\s*.+:`: PIN,
```

That requires at least one character between `key` and `:`. OpenSSH's `ssh` does supply one — #2230, which added these patterns, documents the prompt as `Enter PIN for ${key_type} key ${path_to_key}:`, and that's `sshconnect2.c`:

```c
xasprintf(&prompt, "Enter PIN for %s key %s: ",
    sshkey_type(sign_key), id->filename);
```

But `ssh-keygen` already knows which key it was handed, and names only the type (`ssh-keygen.c`, in the `verify-required` branch):

```c
if (signer == NULL && sshkey_is_sk(signkey)) {
    if ((signkey->sk_flags & SSH_SK_USER_VERIFICATION_REQD)) {
        xasprintf(&prompt, "Enter PIN for %s key: ",
            sshkey_type(signkey));
```

giving `Enter PIN for ED25519-SK key: ` — no path, no match. That asymmetry is why pushing with an sk key has always had a popup and signing never did.

```diff
 		`Enter\s*PIN\s*for\s*'.+':`:              PIN,
+		`Enter\s*PIN\s*for\s*.+:`:                PIN,
```

This can't over-match: `ttyText` is reset at every newline, so the scanner only ever holds the current line. I checked it still ignores `Confirm user presence for key ...` and ordinary git output.

To be clear about scope: this second hunk isn't separately reachable today. Every other call site with a credential strategy (`sync.go`, `remote.go`, `tag.go`) is a network op invoking `ssh`, whose wording carries the path. Only signing goes through `ssh-keygen`, and signing never runs under credential handling. The two changes are really one.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create an sk key with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk -O verify-required` and set it as `user.signingKey` with `gpg.format = ssh`
2. `git config commit.gpgSign true`
3. Commit in lazygit → subprocess terminal
4. Set `git.overrideGpg: true` and commit again → "Git command failed", no prompt

**Expected behavior**

The PIN is collected in the same popup a push uses, with no subprocess terminal.

**Result with both changes**

Popup → PIN → touch → `git log --show-signature` reports a good signature. Covers commit, amend, reword and tag, since all four route through `WithGpgHandling`.

Two notes on the result, neither a blocker for me but worth flagging:

- The touch isn't announced. After the PIN, the status sits on "Committing…" while the key blinks; `Confirm user presence for key ...` matches no pattern. Push behaves the same way today, so it's at least consistent.
- Anything else wanting a TTY during the commit (an interactive pre-commit hook) would now run under lazygit's pty instead of getting the subprocess terminal. I don't have one to test with.

I'm running the two hunks above as a local patch and happy to open a PR if you want it, including whether `overrideGpg` is the right switch for this or whether it should just become the default behaviour.

**Version info**

```
commit=, build date=, build source=nix, version=0.61.1, os=linux, arch=amd64, git version=2.54.0
```

Possibly related: #1146 (GPG signing breaks commit flow), #4668, #3205.

title: Keep copied commits when switching to another worktree or repo
body:
If you copy commits with shift-C and then switch to another worktree, the copied commits are gone, so you can't paste them there with shift-V. This is a common workflow: copy commits from the branch that is checked out in one worktree, maybe drop them there right away, then switch to the worktree of another branch and paste them.

Create the cherry-picking mode once and share it between all repo states. This also lets you paste in a different clone of the same repo, as long as that clone has the copied commits (for example because you fetched them there). If the current repo doesn't have them, git cherry-pick fails with "bad object", and we show this as an error.

title: Fix occasionally failing integration test

labels.name: ignore-for-release

body:
The integration test filter_and_search/search_a_long_diff fails now and then on CI with "Expected search prompt to be focused". Pressing "/" in the focused main view reads the rest of the diff with ReadToEnd. Its callback opens the prompt by enqueueing the work onto the UI thread. ReadToEnd marks its task as done before calling the callback, so for a moment no task is busy. If the idle wait of the test driver wakes up in that moment, the test checks for the prompt before it is open. Adding a sleep between the two calls makes the test fail every time.

The same gap exists when going to the bottom of a view, since that callback enqueues its work onto the UI thread too.

Call the callback first, and mark the task as done after it returns. The work that the callback enqueues holds a task of its own from the moment it is enqueued, so lazygit no longer counts as idle in between.

title: Fix drawing git's diff stat after switching screen modes
body:
Changing the screen mode renders the main view again, and so does anything else that changes its size along with what it shows. With git's own diff, that render laid a commit's diffstat out to the width the view had before. The graph then wrapped onto rows of its own in a view that got narrower, and stopped short in one that got wider.

A diff renderer's render is created after the layout pass, since only the layout settles the view's size, and takes its width there. git's own diff took its width straight away instead, when the render was asked for. Create its task after the layout as well.

This bug is going to be a little more prominent with the upcoming PR series that moves hunk staging to the main view; in that case, when you stage the first hunk into a custom patch, the main view can get split side-by-side, and without this fix the left half of the main view would render its diff stat to the old width of the view.

title: Enable hints for custom commands
body:
### PR Description

Custom commands can now opt into a keybinding hint in the panel footer, like built-in keybindings:

``` yaml
customCommands:
  - key: 'x'
    command: 'git fetch'
    context: 'global'
    description: 'Fetch'
    displayHint: true    # new: shows this command's hint in the panel footer
```

When `displayHint` is `true`, a hint labelled with the command's `description` (falling back to the command itself) is shown in the footer of the panels where the command's context is active.

#### The hint logic mirrors dispatch:

- View-scoped commands show their hint in their own view, ahead of the view's built-in hints; on a key conflict the view-scoped hint wins.
- Global commands show their hint in every view, except when the key is claimed by an enabled view-scoped binding there (that binding wins in dispatch), and they shadow a built-in global binding on the same key.
- Hints are hidden while the search input is focused, since custom commands aren't dispatched there either.

#### Notes:

- Config validation rejects `displayHint` on command menu entries. Only standalone commands that do not have a commandMenu may carry a hint.
- Custom command bindings are now built once per keybinding reset instead of on every footer render.
- Integration test `custom_commands/global_context` covers both scopes, the shadowing case, and search suppression; config validation has unit tests for the new rejection.

title: Theme switcher v2
body:
### PR Description

Fixes #4561

This adds a way to switch between color themes while lazygit is running. Themes are YAML files in a `themes` folder in the config directory. Pressing `#` (also listed under Global in the `?` menu as "Select theme...") opens a menu of them; picking one recolors lazygit immediately and remembers the choice across restarts. No config file has to be edited to switch themes.

I'm opening this as a draft: it's a working prototype for #4561, and I don't expect it to be merged (see CONTRIBUTING.md). It may also be useful to people who want the feature in their own fork. It is based on current master and builds on the recent theme work (#6062, #6063, #6065): theme files use the same `gui.theme` / `gui.darkTheme` / `gui.lightTheme` settings as `config.yml`.

#### How it works

1. Put theme files into `<config dir>/themes/` (`lazygit --print-config-dir` prints the config dir), e.g. `mocha.yml` and `latte.yml`. A theme's name is its file name without `.yml`.
2. Press `#`. The menu lists `(none)` and every theme, with a radio button on the selected one. Choosing one applies it right away and shows the toast `Theme: <name>`.
3. The choice is saved in `selected_theme.yml` next to `state.yml`, so lazygit starts with it the next time.

A theme file is a partial lazygit config that may only contain theme settings:

```yaml
gui:
  theme:
    activeBorderColor: ['#b4befe', bold]
    inactiveBorderColor: ['#a6adc8']
    defaultFgColor: ['#cdd6f4']
    authorColors:
      '*': '#b4befe'
    branchColorPatterns:
      '^feature/': '#f9e2af'
  lightTheme:
    defaultFgColor: ['#4c4f69']
```

#### Design decisions

- **A theme is a config layer.** Precedence: built-in defaults, then the global config file(s) (including `LG_CONFIG_FILE`), then the selected theme, then the per-repo config files, so per-repo colors keep working. As everywhere else, `gui.darkTheme`/`gui.lightTheme` are applied after all layers; a theme file can ship its own, which win over those in `config.yml`.
- **Theme files may only contain `gui.theme`, `gui.darkTheme` and `gui.lightTheme`.** Anything else is an error and the theme isn't applied: other keys (including `gui.colorScheme`), misspelled theme keys, and empty or null values (which would silently wipe the user's own values). YAML anchors, aliases and merge keys work.
- **Theme files are never rewritten.** Files in the older layout (`authorColors`, `branchColorPatterns` or `branchColors` directly under `gui`, as catppuccin's `themes-mergable` files have) are converted in memory with the same code that migrates `config.yml`.
- **The selection isn't written to `config.yml`.** lazygit doesn't write the user's config file, so the menu saves the choice in a state file of its own. It isn't stored in `state.yml`, because every running lazygit instance rewrites that file as a whole, which would undo a choice made in another instance.
- **Selecting a theme only applies the theme.** It loads the new layer, copies just the theme settings into the live config and re-applies the colors through the same code that runs when the terminal's background changes. Selected tabs and runtime toggles (branch sort order, graph, whitespace) survive a switch.
- **Editing the active theme file** takes effect when lazygit regains focus, like edits of `config.yml`.
- **A broken theme never blocks startup.** A selected theme that can't be loaded falls back to no theme; an error toast names it, the menu marks it `(not loaded)` with the reason as its tooltip, and choosing it again shows the full error. A theme whose file has disappeared shows as `(not found)`.
- **Key `#`:** it's free in every context on every platform, arrives unmodified from all terminals and keyboard layouts I checked (including AltGr), and hints at hex colors. It has to be quoted in YAML (`selectTheme: '#'`).

#### Relation to #4561

- Themes folder in the config directory: yes.
- Active theme: chosen from the menu and kept in a state file rather than in a config option (reason above).
- Shortcut to pick a theme: yes, as a dedicated theme menu; it could become an entry of a general settings menu later.

#### Fixes and refactors along the way

Switching themes at runtime makes several existing problems routine, so they come first, as separate commits. Where possible, a commit demonstrating the bug (EXPECTED/ACTUAL) precedes its fix.

- Custom commands were duplicated for every additional config file without a `customCommands` key (per-repo config files, further `LG_CONFIG_FILE` entries).
- Merge keys (`<<: *palette`) in `branchColorPatterns` were read as a pattern named `<<`, and the merged patterns were lost.
- A toast raised just before a waiting status (such as "Fetching…" at startup) was hidden behind it; toasts now show ahead of waiting statuses.
- Data races between worker goroutines and theme state: branch-name suggestion labels, the command log, plain patch formatting, and gocui copying a view's colors for broken escape sequences.
- The graph's color cache grew with every color change.
- Re-applying the theme after the terminal's background changes also reset view titles (e.g. the commit files title lost its commit); it now only sets the views' colors.
- The frame color of an active search or filter was lost when a reloaded config changed the colors, and earlier command log lines kept the previous text color.

Changes users without theme files may notice: toasts show ahead of waiting statuses; custom commands are no longer duplicated; merge keys in `branchColorPatterns` work; the list of migration changes printed at startup may be in a slightly different order.

#### Testing

- Unit tests for loading, validation, old-layout conversion, precedence (including the dark/light overrides and pattern order), fallback, persistence and switching, and tests for each fix.
- 19 integration tests in `pkg/integration/tests/theme/`: the menu and the keybindings menu, the theme at startup, broken and missing themes, per-repo overrides, dark/light overrides in a theme file, reload on focus, runtime settings and view titles kept across a switch, and recoloring of the commits, staging and merge conflicts views.
- The full integration suite passes (591 tests), also with the race detector (no data races reported).
- Manual testing: I run an Isolated docker instance of the repo with a demo repo and multiple themes I tried the switching of themes and tested the cases of corrupted files.

#### How to review

The commits are meant to be read one at a time: bug fixes first, then behavior-preserving refactors (a helper for files next to `state.yml`, extracting the migration of theme keys, extracting `reapplyTheme` and `applyViewColors`), then the theme layer, the load-error toast, `AppConfig.SelectTheme`, the menu, and the docs (new "Themes" section in `docs-master/Config.md`).

#### Known limitations

- Themes don't change the terminal's background color; lazygit doesn't control it (documented, with a pointer to `{{colorScheme}}` for diff renderers).
- Only `.yml` files directly in the `themes` folder are listed (no subfolders).
- After a theme failed to load at startup, fixing its file takes effect when it's chosen again, on a repo switch or on restart, not on focus.
- For old-layout files, error messages refer to the converted content (the error says so).
- No live preview while moving through the menu.

#### How this was made

I built this with an AI coding agent (Claude Code). I made the design decisions listed above, and every commit went through a separate review before the next one was started. I'm happy to answer questions about any part of it.

body:
This was an attempt to make lazygit's overall UI look more "elegant", but it has too many problems. The biggest is that we have panels that combine two views (e.g. a prompt with suggestions below, or the commit message editor with subject and body), and showing the frame of the inactive half of these as "dim" looks wrong; we'd have to add a new concept of a view that doesn't have the focus but otherwise still looks active.

Also, some terminals don't do a good job of showing lines made of dim box drawing characters (e.g. Zed's builtin terminal). This could probably be improved by using a grey hex color instead of dim, but then we'd have to pick one that looks good with all possible terminal color scheme.

That's too many questions, and it's not important enough to spend time on this, so just revert the change.

title: docs: remove dead GitArbor TUI link
body: The `cadamsdev/gitarbor-tui` repository no longer exists (404), but the README's related-projects list still links to it. Removes the bullet. Docs-only change; DCO signed off.

title: Make shift-backspace do the same as backspace in editors
body:
This can be useful when typing an all-caps word; if you mistype one letter, you can delete it without having to let go of shift.

Closes #6076.

title: Improve the rendering of the commit graph for terminals that support it
body: Lazygit uses box drawing characters to render the commit graph. This is problematic, because not all possible graph topologies can be represented by them. In the example below, the first merge commit is the parent of two more commits, a1 and b1, but you can't see this in the left image; it looks like a1's parent was x1. Improve this by using kitty's branch drawing characters that were added to kitty in https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/pull/7681. Ghostty, Contour and VS Code's builtin terminal support them too; WezTerm supports them in a nightly build. Lazygit uses them automatically when it can tell that the terminal supports them, which is the case for Ghostty and kitty, but not VS Code or Contour; if you are using a terminal that supports them but isn't recognized (or if you happen to use a font that contains them), you can opt in by setting the new `gui.commitGraphStyle` config to "detailed". The little circles that represent commits look nicer too. | Before | After | | ------ | ----- | | | |

title: Make Shift + Backspace still delete characters
body:
Whenever I edit a commit message, I often find myself writing a word, then wanting to backspace it. If I capitalize something I am used to just hold down the Shift key while backspacing (say, if I tag my commit messages like [FEAT] or [FIX]). When holding down the Shift-Key in the commit edit window however, the backspace-key does nothing. I'd expect it to just work still, like it does in any other text editor.

So my feature-request is rather simple: Holding down the shift-key should make it so that backspace is not affected and still works just fine. I don't see how that could conflict with other key bindings.

I tried to see if I could find what specifically triggers this within your code-base, but didn't really find _the_ spot to change.

title: Allow copying multiple range-selected items
body:

title: Allow copying multiple commit hashes with <c-o>
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When I multi-select commits in the commits panel and press `Ctrl+O` (copy commit hash), lazygit shows:

```text
Disabled: Action does not support range selection, please select a single item.
```

It would be useful if copying commit hashes supported multiple selected commits. Copying multiple hashes seems like an action that naturally works with range selection.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Allow `Ctrl+O` to copy the hashes of all selected commits when multiple commits are selected.

For example, if three commits are selected, their hashes could be copied one per line:

```text
abc123...
def456...
789abc...
```

Optionally, the same could apply to branch names when using `Ctrl+O` in the branches panel.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

One workaround is to use a custom `git log` command such as `allBranchesLogCmds`, for example:

```text
git log --graph --color=always --abbrev-commit --decorate --pretty="%Cred%h%Creset -%C(auto)%d%Creset %s %Cgreen(%ar) %C(bold blue)<%an>%Creset"
```

Then I can press `1` to open the log output and manually select/copy the hashes with the mouse.

For example:

```text
* 21eeb24 - feat(vim): add opencode terminal keymap (5 months ago) <Risyanggi Azmi Faizin>
* a8abe42 - feat(vim): change copy path to fp, and support range (7 months ago) <Risyanggi Azmi Faizin>
* 538ff05 - feat(zsh): add alias oc=opencode (8 months ago) <Risyanggi Azmi Faizin>
* 32fa5d9 - chore(vim): update without crashing (8 months ago) <Risyanggi Azmi Faizin>
* 309e170 - feat(vim): remove cp mapping for markdown preview (8 months ago) <Risyanggi Azmi Faizin>
```

This works, but it requires leaving the normal commit selection flow and manually selecting the hashes from the log output. It would be more convenient if `Ctrl+O` could simply copy the hashes from the commits currently selected in the commits panel.

### Additional context

This is mainly about copying commit hashes from multiple selected commits. I haven't run into a strong need for the other `y` options to support range selection. Copying multiple branches is a bonus.

Happy to provide more details if needed.

title: Change the demo gifs to videos and update them for the newly added features
body:
The demo videos were rendered as animated gifs, which is less than ideal, because they start playing automatically, they loop but users can't tell when they start over from the beginning, and they can't be paused or rewound.

Convert them to videos instead so that users see a playhead and the usual player controls. Leave a bit of room at the bottom for those controls; different browsers render those differently, so it's a bit of a best effort solution.

Also take this opportunity to update some of the demos for the changed functionality of #6035, #6039 and others.

title: Toggle for `--no-verify` for all actions
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I often have to perform some action which conflicts with pre-commit hooks.

For a simple commit, I can use <kbd>w</kbd> which does a `git commit --no-verify`.

But for all other actions (amend, rebase, patches, whatever), I must do the work from the terminal instead.

### Describe the solution you'd like
It would be nice to have a "global override" for `--no-verify`.

It could be similar to how there is a global override for wrapping via <kbd>ctrl+w</kbd>. That shows `[ignoring whitespace]` in the top right corner.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Doing it from the terminal.

### Additional context
Thanks for considering it!

title: Delete or push multiple tags at once
body: Make it possible to range-select multiple tags and delete or push them all at once.

title: Offer to pull all branches in a stack when pulling the topmost one
body:
When somebody else rebases a stack of branches and force-pushes it, pulling the topmost branch leaves the branches below it diverged. Since #6067 they can be updated manually with `f`, but pushing the stack offers to push the branches
below along with the current one, so pulling should be symmetric, and this PR adds that.

title: Auto-forward branches even if checked out in another worktree
body:
Lazygit can auto-forward main branches after fetching, which is useful to always keep your `main` branch up to date. However, checking out `main` in another worktree stopped this from happening, on the assumption that we don't want to touch branches that are checked out somewhere. For a main branch this is not an issue (as long as the worktree doesn't have modified files); forwarding it in that case too is useful for the setup where you always keep main checked out in the main worktree, and work on feature branches in linked worktrees.

Pressing `f` on such a branch already supported fast-forwarding it even when checked out in a worktree, so now auto-forwarding after fetching does the same.

title: Use `f` to "fast-forward" branches whose upstream branch was rewritten
body:
Lazygit shows local branches that have diverged from their upstream with a yellow `↓3↑5`. There can be two reasons for diverging, and right now it's impossible to tell which of these is the case: (1) you rebased the branch locally (or rewrote its history), in which case you want to force-push it, or (2) someone else rebased the branch, in which case you want to pull it. (We'll ignore the case where both of these happened, in which case you need to manually reconcile the work that each side did, e.g. through cherry-picking; you want to avoid this situation.)

With this PR, lazygit distinguishes the two scenarios, and for (2) it shows the `↓3↑5` in a dim yellow. What's more, you don't even have to check out the branch to pull it; you can press `f` to reset it to its upstream without checking it out, like you would fast-forward a branch that is behind its upstream. In fact the command is still called "Fast-forward", which is technically not quite correct, but it feels the same to me. Fast-forwarding a diverged branch in this way is very useful if an entire stack of branches was rebased remotely; you can simply range-select all those branches and hit `f` to bring them up to date with their upstreams.

title: Add a keybinding for collapsing the directory the cursor is in
body:
I've read CONTRIBUTING.md, and I know this project doesn't accept pull requests.
I'm opening this one anyway, so let me be upfront about why.

I wanted this feature badly enough to build it for my own daily use.

If it isn't to your taste, please just close it — no explanation needed, and no hard feelings. I'll keep using it in my fork either way. But I do hope that something like this makes it into lazygit one day.

### PR Description

Working in a deeply nested directory and wanting to fold it away means first walking the cursor up to the directory's own line and only then collapsing it. This binds that to a single key, leaving the cursor on the directory that was just collapsed so it can be repeated to fold up the tree one level at a time.

The containing directory is found by scanning upwards for the first item rendered at a smaller visual depth, rather than by taking the parent of the selected item's path. Paths don't survive either of the tree's display transformations: a chain of single-child directories is compressed into one node whose path names the deepest of them, so the path's parent is often a node that doesn't exist, and with showRootItemInFileTree disabled the internal paths carry no "./" prefix. Visual depth is exactly what's on screen, so both fall out for free.

title: Add dark and light color themes
body:
Make it possible to override `gui.theme` colors for light or dark backgrounds, by setting them in `gui.darkTheme` or `gui.lightTheme`, respectively; this is often necessary when there isn't a single color that looks good in both.

Use this to provide better defaults for the background color of a selected line, and to add a color for the background of an inactive selected line (used in unfocused views), which didn't have one by default.

Also, provide a way to turn off the "bold" highlighting of the selected line, which was hard-coded and couldn't be changed; there's a new config setting `gui.theme.selectedLineFgColor` that is `[bold]` by default (so existing behavior is unchanged), but can be set to `[default]` to remove the bold. This addresses #2304.

title: Allow telling diff renderers whether the terminal is dark or light
body:
Renderers like delta and difftastic pick their colors for either a dark or a light background, and they can't find out which one the terminal has, because lazygit runs them with TERM=dumb, and in a pty that doesn't answer their queries.

Add `{{colorScheme}}` to the commands of diff renderers. It is 'dark' or 'light', based on what the terminal reports (which can be overridden by `gui.colorScheme` if the terminal doesn't support the query). It can be passed to delta as `--{{colorScheme}}` and to difftastic as `--background={{colorScheme}}`; other renderers can choose between options with a template expression.

title: Improve the randomly picked author colors
body:
Lazygit automatically picks random colors for the authors in the Commits log. On a dark terminal theme, many of these were too dark and barely readable; this can also be seen in the demo videos on the lazygit entry page. Improving this is not trivial, because a range of colors that looks good on a dark background comes out too pale on a light background.

To improve this, detect the terminal's background color (with a config override for those terminals that don't report it), and pick different ranges of colors depending on that. In later PRs we will use the same background detection to allow passing `--dark` or `--light` to a diff renderer, and to support different `gui.theme` configurations for light and dark.

While at it, fix the problem that the `gui.authorColors` config for manually overriding some of the random colors didn't update on a config reload.

title: Keep coverage errors out of the output of the pipeline tests

labels.name: ignore-for-release
labels.description: This will exclude the PR from release notes

body:
On the Windows CI job,
TestStartPipelineReadsWhatTheCommandsComplainAbout fails now and then because the output it reads has an extra line after the expected one. The line starts with "error: coverage meta-data emit failed" and ends with "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process."

The pipeline tests run the test binary itself as the members of the pipeline. CI builds it with -cover, and the members inherit GOCOVERDIR from go test, so each of them writes coverage data to that directory when it calls os.Exit. The meta-data file has the same name for every process of one binary, and every process replaces it by renaming a new copy onto it. (Go's check for an existing file compares its size against the wrong length, so it never finds one.) On Windows this rename fails if another process holds the file open. In this test both members exit at the same time, and the runtime prints the failure to stderr. StartPipeline puts every member's stderr into the output that the test compares.

Exit the members with syscall.Exit instead. It skips the runtime's exit hooks, so the members write no coverage data at all. Nothing is lost by this. Their coverage data went to a temporary directory of go test, not to the directory that CI uploads.

This fixes a regression introduced with #6025.

title: Commits panel: checkout fails for a branch in another worktree
body:
Since #4117, pressing `space` on a commit offers to check out a branch that points at it. If another worktree has that branch checked out, the checkout fails with git's error. The Branches panel asks to switch to that worktree instead.

I have a fix with an integration test on my fork: https://github.com/seflue/lazygit/tree/worktree-aware-checkout-from-commits. It reuses the Branches panel's prompt and stays in the Commits panel after the switch.

Closes #6056.

When trying to edit a dir, it should open it in the editor defined in editPreset

title: Staging pannel goes inactive when fully maximized
body:
## Describe the bug

When using the separate **Staged changes / Unstaged changes** panels, the **Staged changes** panel becomes gray/inactive when it is fully maximized.

The panel can be maximized through the intermediate screen modes normally. The problem occurs specifically when reaching the final/full maximization state using `Ctrl+`.

This appears to be a regression introduced in **lazygit 0.60.0**. Versions **0.59.0 and earlier work correctly**.

## To Reproduce

1. Open a Git repository in lazygit.
2. Modify a file.
3. Stage the file.
4. Select the **Staged changes** panel.
5. Press `Ctrl+` to increase the panel's screen mode.
6. Continue pressing `Ctrl+` until the final/full maximization state is reached.
7. Observe that the Staged changes panel becomes gray/inactive.

## Expected behavior

The Staged changes panel should remain active and usable when fully maximized, just as it does in the preceding screen modes.

## Actual behavior

At the final/full maximization state, the Staged changes panel becomes gray/inactive.

It still occupies the full screen, but it appears to lose focus and cannot be interacted with normally.

The problem is specific to the separate staged/unstaged panel layout. Using the single Main view does not exhibit this behavior.

## Screenshots

See attached screenshot.

## Version info

### Affected

```text
lazygit 0.60.0 and later
```

The issue is reproducible with the current version as well:

```text
commit=0134df802366186633176dd2e093a25a1d56c199
build date=2026-09-06T02:37:12Z
build source=unknown
version=0134df80
os=linux
arch=amd64
git version=2.52.0
```

### Working

```text
lazygit 0.59.0 and earlier
```

I have verified that versions before 0.60.0 do not exhibit this behavior.

## Additional context

It seems that this issue is not present in the master, so it might have been already fixed. However I found other problems in master that were also reported.

https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/5974#issuecomment-5804429217

title: Changing the diff context size in the staging view exits it back to the files panel
body:
### Describe the bug

Pressing `}` or `{` (increase/decrease diff context size) while focused in the staging view (line-by-line view entered with `<enter>` on a file) silently drops out of it: the hunk/line cursor is lost and the main view is re-rendered as the plain unfocused diff preview. Pressing `<esc>` then lands in the files panel.

The context size itself is applied correctly — only the view state is lost.

### To Reproduce

1. Modify a file in a repo.
2. Focus the Files panel, select the file, press `<enter>` to enter the staging view.
3. Press `}`.

Observed: toast "Changed diff context size to N", the line cursor disappears, the main view title gains the `[0]` index (i.e. it is no longer the focused staging view).
Expected: the staging view stays focused with the line selection preserved, just re-rendered with the new context size.

Reproduced with `git.diffRenderers` both set (delta) and empty, so it is not pager-related.

### Cause

`pkg/gui/controllers/context_lines_controller.go`, `applyChange()`:

```go
currentContext := self.c.Context().CurrentSide()
switch currentContext.GetKey() {
// we make an exception for our staging and patch building contexts because they actually need to refresh their state afterwards.
case context.PATCH_BUILDING_MAIN_CONTEXT_KEY:
	self.c.Refresh(types.RefreshOptions{Scope: []types.RefreshableView{types.PATCH_BUILDING}})
case context.STAGING_MAIN_CONTEXT_KEY, context.STAGING_SECONDARY_CONTEXT_KEY:
	self.c.Refresh(types.RefreshOptions{Scope: []types.RefreshableView{types.STAGING}})
default:
	currentContext.HandleRenderToMain()
}
```

`ContextMgr.CurrentSide()` (`pkg/gui/context.go:246`) walks the context stack and returns the first context whose kind is `types.SIDE_CONTEXT`. The staging and patch-building contexts are main contexts, not side contexts, so those two `case` arms can never match. The `default` arm therefore runs and calls `HandleRenderToMain()` on the files panel, which overwrites the staging view.

The patch-building case is usually masked by `checkCanChangeContext()`, which refuses the change while `PatchBuilder.Active()`, but the same dead-branch problem applies when the patch builder is not yet active.

### Version info

lazygit 0.65.1 (Homebrew), git 2.54.0, macOS 15 (arm64).

### Note

title: Avoid showing pull request icons with a delay on startup even though they are cached
body:
When lazygit starts up in a repo with many remote branches, the pull request icons in the branches panel showed up a good while after the branch list itself, even though the pull requests come from the cache file and are in the model before the first render. In the repo where this showed up (5400 remote branches) the icons were up to half a second late.

The icons are rendered from Model.PullRequestsMap, and that map is built from the remotes' URLs, because a branch's upstream remote tells us which repo owner's pull requests to look for. The map therefore stays empty until the remotes are in the model, and the remotes refresh doesn't put them there until it has also enumerated and sorted all remote branches. In a big repo that takes hundreds of milliseconds; reading the remotes themselves takes ten.

Load the two separately, and put the remotes in the model as soon as they have been read from the git config. The branches refresh then finds them there, and the pull request icons are part of the first render of the branch list.
